newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Five out of seven Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA) councillors resigned on Thursday, but they first suspended controverisal CEO Harris Gxaweni for "non performance,"
- Civil sanctions of three times the amount gained through insider trading, and criminal liability of two million rand or 10 years in prison, has been recommended by the insider trading task group.

- SA was considering putting in place a 1,5 billion dollar syndicated loan facility for three years to draw down at times when there was pressure on the foreign exchange reserves, foreign banking sources said on Thursday.

- President Nelson Mandela, after meeting Zairean rebel alliance leader Laurent Kabila in Tuynhuys last night, submitted proposals to Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko on the handover of power to a transitional authority.
- SA Revenue Service CEO Piet Liebenberg has resigned, apparently due to irreconcilable differences with the finance ministry over the status of the tax collection agency.
BUSINESS REPORT

- NBS is facing legal action, not only from investors affected by the 137 million rand fraud at its Kempton Park branch discovered earlier this year, but also from the property developers who are believed to have borrowed funds from the controversial bridging fianance scheme run by the branch manager Vito Assante and attorney Nick Nel.

- Cape Produce, the investor that blew the whistle on the controversial NBS Kempton Park fraud and which is also its largest investor at 30 million rand, is suing NBS for refusing to repay its investment, it was disclosed this week.

- Dramatic changes to the way insider trading is defined and prosecuted were on Thursday recommended by the Insider Trading Task Group, which includes representatives of most South African financial bodies.
- Banking group Nedcor reported a "conservative" 24 percent intermin growth in earnings per share for the half year to March 31, Richard Laubscher, the group's executive, said on Thursday.

- The Chamber of Mines said on Thursday it was still waiting for Penuell Maduna, the mineral and energy affairs minister, to respond officially to the draft green paper on the future of mineral rights policy presented to him last October.
SAKE BEELD
- The new proposed legislation to regulate insider trading showed its teeth yesterday.
- South Africa showed the highest increase in the Producter Price Index in 21 months in March.
- Nail spoke to Gencor first before it considered bidding for an interest in Goldfields.
THE STAR

- The Independent Broadcasting Authority was plunged into disarray last night when five of its seven councillors resigned just hours after the council unanimously voted to suspend IBA chief executive officer Harris Gxaweni.
- Police arrested four men in Hillbrow on Thursday soon after the senseless murder of a 77-year-old security guard outside a house in Observatory, Johannesburg.
- South African Revenue Service chief executive Piet Liebenberg resigned late last night, a Finance Ministry spokesman said.
- An emotional Archbishop Desmond Tutu said on Thursday that National Party leader F W de Klerk's submission to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission had almost made him cry.
